contributions.detail: Two Schedule A sheets. PDF p3 carries 8 entries — each occupying TWO printed lines, the name and amount on one and the address continuation on the next — summing 72.52 + 57.66 + 96.50 + 92.00 + 500.00 + 250.00 + 500.00 + 96.80 = 1,665.48, its own printed page subtotal to the cent. PDF p4 carries 3 entries summing 250.00 + 200.00 + 279.02 = 729.02, its own printed subtotal to the cent. 1,665.48 + 729.02 = 2,394.50 = the printed grand total = the cover's promoted per-period Column A cell. The balance ladder closes as well: line 3 beginning 0 + line 4 2,394.50 = line 5 2,394.50; minus line 6 2,364.33 = line 7 30.17. THE LOAN QUESTION was run through the ladder, not read off the word (§B3): line 5 of p3 is the candidate's own '(loan)' of 500.00, and it IS an itemized contribution row here — the cover books nothing at line 3 (beginning balance is a written 0), so there is no beginning-balance slot for it, and without it the page falls 500.00 short of its own printed 1,665.48. Column B prints the same 2,394.50 and is never summed as an increment.

expenditures.detail: Two Schedule B sheets, the same two-lines-per-entry layout. PDF p5 carries 8 entries summing 766.57 + 250.00 + 29.85 + 29.85 + 89.25 + 6.54 + 100.00 + 692.27 = 1,964.33 = its own printed subtotal to the cent. PDF p6 carries 3 entries summing 100.00 + 100.00 + 200.00 = 400.00 = its own printed subtotal. 1,964.33 + 400.00 = 2,364.33 = the printed grand total = Column A. in_kind_convention: monetary-only — tested on BOTH sides of THIS filing (§G1). Neither schedule prints an in-kind column and no row carries an in-kind marking, so the two conventions give identical sums (2,394.50 and 2,364.33) and both close on the printed figures.
escalation_note: EIGHT tight-crop escalations, and one of them reversed a first reading. (1) PDF p3 line 1's amount read as '77.52' in a tight 1200 dpi crop, which would have made the page sum 1,670.48 against a printed subtotal of 1,665.48. A WIDER 1400 dpi crop showing the whole row rendered it as '72.52' — this filer's cursive 2 has a long flat base stroke that a narrow crop clips into a 7-like form — and the page then closes EXACTLY. Both the wider render and the arithmetic agree, and the arithmetic is decisive under the Rhodes rule; 72.52 is recorded. (2) and (3) the p3 subtotal and the p4 subtotal/total were cropped at 1200 dpi and read 1,665.48 / 729.02 / 2,394.50, three printed figures that are mutually consistent (1,665.48 + 729.02 = 2,394.50) and equal to Column A, so the anchor is corroborated three ways INSIDE this document. (4) and (5) the two '96.x0' cells on p3 (lines 5 and 15) were cropped at 1600 dpi and compared against each other: the page's arithmetic constrains the PAIR to 193.30, i.e. one is 96.50 and the other 96.80, and the glyphs assign 96.50 to line 5 and 96.80 to line 15 (line 5's post-decimal digit is an open 5 with a flat top bar; line 15's has a closed upper bowl). Swapping them would change no total, and both rows say so. (6)-(8) the geometry proof crops recorded in the frames. Nothing was nudged and no figure was changed to make a sum work.

Andrew McCullough' (handwritten), party 'Libertarian' — the second third-party candidate in this chunk — residence Lehi; Office Seeking written 'County Attorney', which agrees with index.csv's channel label. index.csv names no candidate; the page face supplies it. Report type 'Seven days preceding the General Election'; the amendment question is answered 'No' (the options are printed as CIRCLES on this blank and the No circle is struck through); signed and dated 10/27/18; THE CLERK'S 'For Office Use Only' BOX IS ENTIRELY EMPTY — no received stamp of any kind. FORM STOCK — A MIXED-TEMPLATE FILING: the cover is the OLD 'county-only' blank (eagle seal, 'FINANCIAL CAMPAIGN REPORT FOR COUNTY CANDIDATES', Utah County Code 2-5-2 & 17-16-6.5) — the same October-2018 use of the 2-5-2 stock as the Lee filing in this chunk — while all four inner sheets are strap-lined '2016 County & Local School Board Candidates', i.e. leftover 2016 stock. Neither predicts the other (§F6/§G4), and the year is not reclassified. Schedule A heads its payee column 'Name of Contributor' and Schedule B heads its own 'Name/Nature of Expenditure' — the third of the four Schedule-B vocabularies — with no Purpose column on either. DOCUMENT SHAPE: 6 pages = cover / SUMMARY PAGE / Schedule A ×2 / Schedule B ×2. Every Page/of, Last Name and Date of Report box on all five inner sheets is BLANK — a tenth foliation practice for the running tally, and the reason each schedule sheet had to be classified from its own printed heading. THE LAYOUT PROPERTY THAT GOVERNS EVERY ROW INDEX HERE: this filer writes each entry across TWO printed lines — date, name and amount on the first, the address continuation on the second — so 8 entries fill 16 of the 17 lines on p3 and p5, and the even-numbered lines carry an address with an empty amount cell. Every `row` in this record is the line the AMOUNT sits on, and the continuation lines were crop-checked as empty rather than assumed. ROW-INDEX TRAPS SCREENED: no skipped first line on any of the four schedules (the §A1 control rendered the recorded row-1 figure on each), no banner and no voided ROW — though two struck-out figures do appear inside continuation lines and are recorded on their entries; the §B5 one-past control rendered an empty band or the printed subtotal on every page; and no band was ~2x pitch, so no doubled band (§F6/§H3). GEOMETRY HAZARD: pp3-4 are skewed -0.8/-0.9 deg with over 1 pct drift, so the full-width rule list is displaced in the amount column and the `--col` recovery was required there; pp5-6 are square enough to use the full-width ladder. FIELD-SHIFT SCREEN: columns assigned by CONTENT against each sheet's printed headings; dates, names, addresses and money all sit in their own columns and no inversion of the §F2/§G3 kind occurs. PRIVACY: this filing is NOT redacted and prints full mailing lines for donors and vendors alike; every one was reduced to city/state at READ TIME on the contributions side, expenditure rows carry no address field at all in this record, and no street line was written into any field or note.
